story: Thursday afternoon in Sumter Oaks is breezy and clear at 78 degrees, and Gary is making his way toward Town Hall with a determined stride. Over at the Rec Center, Donna is booking a court for two hours with Gary in mind, while Hal sits on his porch wiping down a chair he plans to carry over to Rosa's. Rosa, content on Magnolia Loop, is pinning a note to the street bulletin board inviting everyone to a welcome dinner at her place on Saturday at six, with Gary, Hal, and Donna already confirmed.
events: Donna (court reservation kiosk): Reserve a court for Gary and me, two hours max
Hal (hal porch chair): Check the chair is sturdy and wipe it down to carry over to Rosa's
Rosa (street bulletin board): Pin up a note: welcome dinner at Rosa's, Saturday at 6, Gary, Hal and Donna confirmed.

gary.thought_process: I'm in Town Square, nobody around, and I've been stalling on the Architectural Review paperwork for the cart lights and sound system. My reflections say I'm finally filing it today so Hal can drop the matter. Town Hall connects from here, and L-01 requires approval for visible exterior modifications. Filing now gets the cart legal before the parade. Dinner setup at Rosa's isn't until around five-thirty, so I've got time. Head to Town Hall.

parameters.content: Going to file the Architectural Review paperwork for my cart lights and sound system before I talk myself out of it again.

donna.thought_process: I'm at the rec center and nobody's around. Last tick I checked the ladder board, and I signed Pruitt-Kowalski up back at tick 83, so I want to see how we're placed before the match. Gary should be along any minute, and I'll handle the paperwork while he warms up. I need to keep my competitive streak productive, not repeat myself. Reserving a court for our practice before the match makes sense since the courts are free right now, and the kiosk caps us at 2 hours, which is plenty.

parameters.content: Reserve a court for Gary and me, two hours max

hal.thought_process: I'm home at Hal's House with no one around. Rosa wants the sturdy chair and a second pair of hands at five-thirty, and I promised cornbread. The chair is right here as hal_porch_chair, so now's the time to get it ready to haul over. The violation reports can wait; Gary filed his paperwork and a clean slate for Saturday suits me fine. Check the chair is sound before I carry it to Rosa's.

parameters.content: Check the chair is sturdy and wipe it down to carry over to Rosa's

rosa.thought_process: All three are confirmed for Saturday at six: Gary and Donna said yes at tick 49, and Hal said yes with cornbread and his chair at tick 153. Nobody is in sight right now, and there's no one to ask or thank. The street bulletin board is a good low-effort way to put the dinner where neighbors will see it. I can also use it to note the five-thirty setup help, so nothing slips. It keeps the dinner moving without pestering anyone I've already pinned down.

parameters.content: Pin up a note: welcome dinner at Rosa's, Saturday at 6, Gary, Hal and Donna confirmed.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
